categories.main_business_segments: Amkor operates as a single business segment focused on outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) services. Its offerings are categorized into Advanced Products (including flip chip, wafer-level, and memory packaging and test services) and Mainstream Products (wirebond packaging and related test services). Advanced Products accounted for approximately 82% of 2024 net sales, while Mainstream Products contributed about 18%.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Amkor's core technologies include advanced semiconductor packaging (such as flip chip, wafer-level chip scale packaging, 2.5D, system-in-package, and high-density fan-out), as well as a broad range of test services. The company leverages high-volume manufacturing processes, wafer bumping, wafer probe, package design, system-level and final test, and drop shipment. It is a leader in developing innovative packaging solutions for miniaturization, heterogeneous integration, and high-performance computing, including SiP, SWIFT, WLFO, and advanced power modules.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Amkor serves integrated device manufacturers (IDMs), fabless semiconductor companies, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), and contract foundries. Its key end markets are communications (smartphones, tablets), computing (data centers, PCs, storage), automotive and industrial (ADAS, electrification, infotainment), and consumer electronics (AR/gaming, wearables, connected home). In 2024, its ten largest customers accounted for 72% of net sales, with Apple and Qualcomm representing 30.8% and 10.2% respectively.
categories.geographic_coverage: Amkor operates globally with manufacturing, R&D, and sales facilities in Asia (China, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Philippines, Taiwan, Vietnam), Europe (Portugal), and the United States. The company’s broad geographic footprint enables it to support regional supply chain needs and mitigate risks. In 2024, the U.S. accounted for about 63% of net sales by customer headquarters, with the remainder from Asia and Europe.
categories.supply_chain_position: Amkor operates in the midstream and downstream segments of the semiconductor supply chain, providing assembly, packaging, and test services after wafer fabrication. It does not manufacture silicon wafers but receives them from customers or foundries, adding value through packaging and testing before shipment to end customers or OEMs.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Amkor’s strategic priorities include leadership in advanced packaging technologies, expanding its geographic footprint (notably with new facilities in Vietnam and Arizona), and optimizing asset utilization. R&D focuses on multi-die integration (2.5D, SWIFT, SiP), wafer- and panel-level packaging, automotive applications, and sustainable packaging solutions. The company collaborates closely with customers to co-develop next-generation packaging and test solutions, with R&D spending of $163 million in 2024.
categories.revenue_model: Amkor generates revenue primarily through turnkey manufacturing services, including semiconductor packaging and test services. Revenue is recognized as services are rendered, typically over a two- to three-week period, and is billed upon completion of each service or combined offering. The company does not take ownership of customer wafers, and its revenue is closely tied to customer demand and utilization rates.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Amkor faces competition from established OSAT providers (ASE Technology, JCET Group, Powertech Technology), contract foundries (TSMC, Samsung), and electronics manufacturing service providers (Universal Scientific Industrial, Luxshare). It also competes with the internal packaging and test capabilities of IDMs. Amkor is positioned as the largest U.S.-headquartered OSAT, with strengths in advanced packaging, geographic diversity, and long-standing customer relationships.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, Amkor reported net sales of $6.3 billion, a 2.9% decrease from 2023, reflecting cyclical industry trends and lower sales in automotive and communications markets. Gross margin was 14.8%, and net income attributable to Amkor was $354 million. The company maintains a strong liquidity position with $1.6 billion in cash and short-term investments, and capital expenditures of $744 million (11.8% of net sales) in 2024. Amkor’s growth is driven by advanced packaging demand in high-growth markets, though results are subject to semiconductor industry cycles.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Amkor differentiates itself through technology leadership in advanced packaging and test, a broad and flexible service portfolio, and a geographically diversified manufacturing base. Its value proposition includes enabling miniaturization, higher integration, and faster time-to-market for customers, as well as providing supply chain resilience and cost-effective solutions. The company emphasizes collaborative innovation, high quality, reliability, and the ability to support customers across multiple end markets and geographies.
